newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 6.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

-- The dollar/drachma exchange rate is on the threshold of 300 drachmas with prospects for further increases as the dollar is seen climbing higher in international markets following the Bundesbank's decision not to raise German interest rates.

-- The development ministry along with the association of Greek banks will revise the legal framework on credit cards in September, granting cardholders more rights against issuer credit institutions.

-- The draft 1998 Budget includes substantial increases in revenues and a freeze in the budgets of ministries in real terms. But the ministries of national defense and education are the wild cards on deputy finance minister Nick Chrystodoulakis' new budget calculations.
-- The dollar threatens the strength of the euro, having risen to new record highs against major European currencies, and creates inflationary pressure on Greece.

-- National Mortgage Bank of Greece is headed at full speed for its merger with the National Housing Bank. A common meeting of the boards of the two banks will take place on August 27 and legal procedures will be concluded by year-end. The two banks are expected to jointly post their fiscal 1997 results.

-- The Thessaloniki Stock Exchange will seek the set up of an independent bourse for small-cap enterprises with flexible entry criteria along the lines of London's Alternative Investment Market. Alternatively, the Thesasaloniki bourse will pursue the transfer of the Athens bourse's small-cap Parallel market.

-- The ministries of national economy and development will pass new legislation in September to finance the business plans of around 80 middle-sized industrial units which are expected to be in dire financial straits in the future unless they are aided.

-- The cost of Olympic Airways' relocation to the new Athens airport constructed at Spata is estimated within a 20 percent range from 118 billion drachmas. The airline's management told reporters its operating and financial performance has improved considerably in 1997.

-- A report from Oxford Analytica suggests that the introduction of the euro will deprive Greek banks of a fifth of their commission revenues and will drive Greek businesses into foreign borrowing because Greek banks operate with different interest rate spreads from their European competitors. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
